channel.title: Thomas Sandmann's blog
channel.description: Thomas' personal thoughts, opinions, learnings and code examples

item.title: R 4.5: importing only selected objects & functions from R packages
item.dc:creator: Thomas Sandmann
item.description: On Friday, R version 4.5 was released. If you are curious about what’s new and what’s changed, you might enjoy reading Russ Hyde’s blog post or R’s official list of changes. For me, the introduction of the use() function is the most interesting aspect of this update.

item.title: Compressing single-cell RNA-seq data with run-length encoding and LZW
item.dc:creator: Thomas Sandmann
item.description: I am always looking for ways to communicate genomics analyses to collaborators in a way that allows them to drill down into the data themselves. Stand-alone HTML reports can be opened in any web browser and can support rich visualizations, making them my an indespensible tool in my tool kit.

item.title: Interacting with box cloud storage: the boxr R package
item.dc:creator: Thomas Sandmann
item.description: This week, I learned how to create custom apps within the box cloud storage service, and how to read & write files from within R using the awesome boxr R package.

item.title: Exploring the tidyHeatmap R package
item.dc:creator: Thomas Sandmann
item.description: This week I learned about the tidyHeatmap package, which wraps the functionality of the awesome ComplexHeatmap R package into functions with a tidyverse interface. No more need for pivoting tidy datasets into matrices and back!

item.dc:creator: Thomas Sandmann

item.title: Querying JSON files with AWS Athena and the noctua R package
item.dc:creator: Thomas Sandmann
item.description: This week, I learned how to query JSON files stored on AWS S3 with the noctua R package, an API for the AWS Athena service.

item.title: Interactive volcano plots with the ggiraph R package
item.dc:creator: Thomas Sandmann
item.description: The ggiraph R package is my new favorite way to add interactivity to a ggplot.

item.title: Conditional panels within shiny modules
item.dc:creator: Thomas Sandmann
item.description: The shiny R package includes the conditionalPanel function to show / hide a panel depending on a javascript expression. Today I learned how to use a conditionalPanel within a shiny module.

item.title: Collaborator-friendly volcano plots with ggplot2
item.dc:creator: Thomas Sandmann
item.description: volcano plots are a staple of genomics papers. The ggrastr::geom_point_rast() function enables collaborators to post-process plots in inkscape or Adobe illustrator - without overwhelming the application with tens of thousands of individual points.

item.title: Embedding R into Quarto documents with quarto-webr
item.dc:creator: Thomas Sandmann
item.description: Today I learned how to use the quarto-webr extension to turn a Quarto markdown document into an interactive report that executes R code in the browser and lets readers change the code on the fly!

item.title: Adventures with parquet III: single-cell RNA-seq data and comparison with HDF5-backed arrays
item.dc:creator: Thomas Sandmann
item.description: Today, I learned how to store single-cell RNA-seq data in a parquet file, created the ParquetMatrix class to retrieve them, and I started to compare the performance of reading from parquet and HDF5 files.

item.title: Adventures with parquet II: Implementing the parquetArraySeed S4 class
item.dc:creator: Thomas Sandmann
item.description: Previously, I learned how to export gene expression data from Bioconductor/R objects as parquet files. Today, I am exploring Hervé Pagès’s awesome DelayedArray Bioconductor package to represent data stored in parquet files as R matrices - retrieving only those subsets needed for downstream analysis.

item.title: Adventures with parquet: Storing & quering gene expression data
item.dc:creator: Thomas Sandmann
item.description: Today I explored storing gene expression data in parquet files, and querying them with the arrow, duckdb or sparklyr R packages.

item.title: Organizing sequencing metadata: experimenting with S7
item.dc:creator: Thomas Sandmann
item.description: This week I learned about R’s new S7 object oriented programming (OOP) system by experimenting with classes that represent the main metadata entities of a next-generation sequencing experiment.

item.title: tourrr: Exploring multi-dimensional data
item.dc:creator: Thomas Sandmann
item.description: Today I learned about exploring multivariate data using tours of projections into lower dimensions. The tourr R package makes it easy to experiment with different tours. Let’s go on a grand tour!

item.title: Documenting data wrangling with the dtrackr R package
item.dc:creator: Thomas Sandmann
item.description: Today I learned about Robert Challen’s dtrackr R package. It extends functionality from the tidyverse to track and visualize the data wrangling operations that have been applied to a dataset.

item.title: Lemur: analyzing multi-condition single-cell data
item.dc:creator: Thomas Sandmann
item.description: This week, Constantin Ahlmann-Eltze and Wolfgang Huber published a preprint describing LEMUR, a new approach to analyzing single-cell experiments that include samples from multiple conditions, e.g. drug treatments, disease-status, etc.
